questions.question: India adopted a policy of Import Substitution Industrialisation (ISI) after independence. Which of the following was a common limitation faced by ISI-led strategy by the 1980s?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Technological backwardness**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• By the 1980s, India’s Import Substitution Industrialisation (ISI) strategy faced significant limitations such as **technological backwardness**, which hindered productivity and competitiveness.
 
• The focus on domestic production led to **limited access to advanced global technologies**, impacting innovation and modernization.
 
• Many industries under ISI were protected by high tariffs, creating a **lack of incentive to innovate or improve efficiency**.
 
• Technological stagnation resulted in **poor quality of goods** and inability to meet international standards, further limiting exports.
 
• Countries relying on ISI strategies often struggled with **low industrial diversification**, exacerbating technological deficiencies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Import Substitution Industrialisation (ISI):**

 
 
• ISI is an economic policy aimed at reducing dependency on imports by promoting domestic production of goods.
 
• It was widely adopted by developing countries post-World War II to foster industrial growth and economic independence.
 
 
 
• **Protectionism in ISI:**
 
 
• High import tariffs and quotas were imposed to protect domestic industries.
 
• While it encouraged initial industrial growth, it often led to inefficiency and lack of global competitiveness.
 
 
 
• **Technological Stagnation:**
 
 
• Limited investment in research and development under ISI policies contributed to technological backwardness.
 
• Dependence on outdated technologies restricted productivity and innovation.
 
 
 
• **Shift to Liberalization:**
 
 
• India began liberalizing its economy in 1991, moving away from ISI towards globalization and free-market policies.
 
• This shift aimed to integrate India into the global economy and encourage technological advancements through foreign investments.

questions.question: Rudradaman, who ruled in the middle of second century AD territories of Mathura and Gujarat belonged to which dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shaka**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Rudradaman I** was a prominent ruler of the **Western Kshatrapas**, a branch of the Shaka dynasty, in the middle of the second century AD.
 
• He is known for his rule over regions that included **Mathura, Gujarat, and parts of Malwa and Kathiawar**.
 
• Rudradaman is celebrated for his administrative skills and military achievements, including his victory over the Satavahanas.
 
• He issued the **Junagadh Rock Inscription**, one of the earliest known inscriptions written in Sanskrit, which highlights his achievements and governance.
 
• The Shaka dynasty played a significant role in Indian history, introducing administrative reforms and patronizing art and culture in their territories.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Shaka Dynasty:**

 
 
• The Shakas were a branch of the Scythians who migrated to India and established rule in northwestern and western regions.
 
• They are known as the Western Kshatrapas in Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Junagadh Rock Inscription:**
 
 
• This inscription was commissioned by Rudradaman I around 150 AD.
 
• It records the construction of the Sudarshana Lake and highlights the achievements of Rudradaman.
 
 
 
• **Western Kshatrapas:**
 
 
• The Western Kshatrapas were a line of Indo-Scythian rulers who controlled parts of modern-day Gujarat, Maharashtra, and Madhya Pradesh.
 
• They were contemporaries of the Satavahanas and Gupta Empires.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the Shaka Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Shaka rule came to an end with the rise of the Gupta Empire, particularly under Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya), who defeated the Shaka ruler Rudrasimha III.

questions.question: Uninterrupted and seamless chain of Input Tax Credit (ITC) is a mechanism to avoid cascading of taxes in which of the following taxes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**GST**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Goods and Services Tax (GST)** is a unified indirect tax system implemented in India to **eliminate cascading effects of taxation**.
 
• The concept of **Input Tax Credit (ITC)** under GST allows businesses to claim credit for the tax paid on purchases and use it to offset the tax liability on sales.
 
• GST ensures an **uninterrupted and seamless chain of Input Tax Credit**, reducing the tax burden at each stage of value addition.
 
• ITC under GST is applicable to **both goods and services**, aligning with the “One Nation, One Tax” principle.
 
• This mechanism improves compliance, ensures transparency, and helps in making products and services more competitive in the market.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cascading Tax Effect:**

 
 
• Occurs when tax is levied on a product at every stage of production without credit for the taxes paid in the earlier stages.
 
• GST eliminates this issue by enabling ITC throughout the supply chain.
 
 
 
• **Input Tax Credit (ITC):**
 
 
• ITC allows taxpayers to deduct the tax paid on inputs from the tax payable on final output.
 
• Conditions for availing ITC include possession of tax invoice, receipt of goods/services, and payment of tax to the government.
 
 
 
• **GST Structure:**
 
 
• GST comprises Central GST (CGST), State GST (SGST), and Integrated GST (IGST).
 
• ITC is transferable between CGST and SGST/IGST under specific rules.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of GST:**
 
 
• Creates a unified tax structure across India, boosting ease of doing business.
 
• Reduces tax evasion by integrating tax systems digitally.
 
• Promotes transparency and reduces litigation in tax administration.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct with reference to the industrial use of freon?

options.text: It is used in refrigeration and aerosol production.
It is primarily used in food processing and as a food preservative
It is used as a pesticide and insecticide.
It is used for textile dyeing.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It is used in refrigeration and aerosol production.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Freon** is a trade name for a group of chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs) and related compounds primarily used as refrigerants.
 
• It is widely used in **refrigeration systems** such as air conditioners, refrigerators, and freezers.
 
• Freon is also used in the production of **aerosol propellants** due to its ability to maintain pressure and flow consistency.
 
• The use of Freon has been regulated under international agreements like the **Montreal Protocol** due to its contribution to ozone layer depletion.
 
• Modern refrigeration systems are transitioning to alternative, eco-friendly refrigerants to replace Freon.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs):**

 
 
• CFCs are compounds made up of chlorine, fluorine, and carbon atoms.
 
• They were once widely used in refrigeration, air conditioning, and aerosol sprays.
 
• CFCs are known to cause **ozone depletion** in the stratosphere.
 
 
 
• **Montreal Protocol:**
 
 
• An international treaty signed in 1987 to phase out substances that deplete the ozone layer, including CFCs.
 
• The treaty has been highly successful in reducing the production and consumption of ozone-depleting substances.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact of Freon:**
 
 
• Freon contributes to global warming and ozone layer depletion.
 
• Hydrochlorofluorocarbons (HCFCs) and hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs) are transitional substitutes but are also being phased out due to environmental concerns.
 
 
 
• **Alternative Refrigerants:**
 
 
• Eco-friendly refrigerants like ammonia (NH₃), carbon dioxide (CO₂), and hydrocarbons (e.g., isobutane) are being adopted.
 
• These alternatives have a lower global warming potential (GWP) and no ozone depletion potential (ODP).

questions.question: What is the NISAR satellite, launched in February 2025 and co-developed by ISRO and NASA, designed for?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Earth observation and climate monitoring**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **NISAR** (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar) is a joint Earth observation satellite developed collaboratively by NASA and ISRO.
 
• The satellite is designed to monitor **ecosystem disturbances, natural hazards, and global environmental changes** such as ice sheet dynamics, forest biomass, and agricultural patterns.
 
• Equipped with **dual-frequency radar systems (L-band by NASA and S-band by ISRO)**, NISAR ensures high-resolution imaging capabilities.
 
• The mission aims to deliver critical data for **climate monitoring, disaster management**, and resource mapping globally.
 
• It is set to launch in **February 2025**, marking a significant collaboration in Earth science between the two space agencies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR):**

 
 
• A radar technology that creates high-resolution images of the Earth's surface by emitting and receiving microwave signals.
 
• It is capable of penetrating clouds, vegetation, and even soil, making it useful for all-weather, day-night observations.
 
 
 
• **L-band and S-band Radars:**
 
 
• L-band radar (long wavelength) is ideal for monitoring vegetation and soil moisture, while S-band radar (shorter wavelength) is suited for detecting finer details like ice and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Key Applications of NISAR:**
 
 
• Tracking deforestation, agricultural patterns, and glacier movements.
 
• Monitoring natural disasters like earthquakes, tsunamis, and floods to aid in disaster response.
 
 
 
• **Data Contribution:**
 
 
• NISAR will provide up to 12 terabytes of imaging data daily, supporting global climate studies and environmental monitoring.
 
 
 
• **ISRO-NASA Collaboration:**
 
 
• This partnership strengthens international cooperation in space exploration and enhances the technological capabilities of both agencies.

questions.question: When was municipal governance first introduced in British India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1687**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Municipal governance was first introduced in British India in **1687**, with the establishment of the municipal corporation in **Madras (now Chennai).**
 
• The Madras Municipal Corporation was the **first attempt by the British to introduce local self-governance** in India.
 
• Following Madras, municipal governance was later extended to Bombay and Calcutta in the early 18th century.
 
• The introduction of municipal governance aimed to ensure better administration, sanitation, and infrastructure development in urban centers.
 
• It laid the foundation for modern urban governance in India, which later evolved through subsequent legislative reforms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terminology:**

 
 
• **Municipal Corporation:** It is a form of urban local governance responsible for the administration of cities with large populations.
 
• **Local Self-Governance:** A system of governance where local authorities manage their own affairs independently within the framework of a larger governing system.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of Municipal Governance:**
 
 
• In 1882, Lord Ripon introduced reforms to strengthen local self-governance, often referred to as the "Father of Local Self-Government in India."
 
• The Montague-Chelmsford Reforms (1919) further emphasized the importance of local governance under the provincial governments.
 
 
 
• **Modern Municipal Governance:**
 
 
• The 74th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992 provided a constitutional status to municipalities and introduced the concept of urban local bodies.
 
• It mandated the establishment of municipal corporations, municipal councils, and Nagar Panchayats based on population size.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• Municipal governance in India plays a key role in urban planning, infrastructure development, and the delivery of essential services.
 
• It ensures civic amenities such as water supply, waste management, street lighting, and public health services.

questions.question: Under the SVAMITVA scheme, which modern technology is used to map land ownership in rural India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Drone Surveying**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The SVAMITVA scheme was launched by the Government of India on **April 24, 2020**, to provide rural landowners with property ownership rights.
 
• Under the scheme, **drone technology** is used for **mapping land parcels** in rural areas to create accurate land records.
 
• Drone surveying ensures **high-resolution aerial imagery** that facilitates precision mapping and minimizes disputes related to land ownership.
 
• The maps generated via drones are integrated with **Geographical Information Systems (GIS)** for ease of access and management.
 
• This initiative aims to promote **financial stability in rural areas** by enabling landowners to use their property as collateral for loans and other financial activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Drone Technology**:

 
 
• Drones, also known as unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), are equipped with cameras, sensors, and GPS systems for high-precision surveying and mapping.
 
• They are widely used in agriculture, disaster management, urban planning, and land surveys due to their efficiency and accuracy.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Information System (GIS)**:
 
 
• GIS is a computer-based tool that analyzes and visualizes spatial data. It integrates maps and data layers for better decision-making.
 
• It plays a critical role in land management, urban planning, and environmental monitoring.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of SVAMITVA Scheme**:
 
 
• To create a comprehensive digital record of land ownership in rural India.
 
• To reduce disputes related to land ownership and promote transparency.
 
• To empower rural property owners by enabling them to monetize their assets.
 
 
 
• **Implementation**:
 
 
• The scheme is implemented by the Ministry of Panchayati Raj in collaboration with the Survey of India.
 
• States and Union Territories actively participate in the process of land survey and mapping.

questions.question: Which characteristic of the CPU determines how many instructions it can process per second?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Clock speed**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Clock speed** refers to the number of cycles a CPU can execute per second, usually measured in Hertz (Hz). A higher clock speed indicates a faster CPU.
 
• It directly affects how quickly a processor can process instructions and execute tasks.
 
• Modern CPUs have clock speeds typically measured in gigahertz (GHz), representing billions of cycles per second.
 
• Clock speed is a critical factor for performance, but it must be paired with other components like memory and storage for optimal efficiency.
 
• Overclocking can increase clock speed beyond the manufacturer's specifications, potentially enhancing performance but at the risk of increased heat and reduced stability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cache size:** Refers to the small-sized, high-speed memory located inside the CPU to store frequently accessed data. While it affects performance, it does not determine the number of instructions processed per second.
 
• **Number of registers:** Registers are small storage locations within the CPU used to store data temporarily during execution. While essential for operations, they do not directly dictate processing speed.
 
• **Power consumption:** Indicates the energy required by the CPU during operation. While it impacts efficiency and heat generation, it does not determine instruction execution.
 
• **Pipelining:** A technique used by modern CPUs to execute multiple instructions simultaneously by dividing the execution process into stages, improving overall performance.
 
• **Multi-core processors:** CPUs with multiple cores can process multiple instructions simultaneously, enhancing processing capability, especially for multitasking and parallel processing workloads.

questions.question: What were ‘privy purses’?

options.text: Pensions paid to the princes after integration

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Pensions paid to the princes after integration**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The privy purses were **annual payments made by the Government of India** to former princely rulers after the integration of princely states into independent India.
 
• The payments were part of an agreement during the integration process, ensuring **economic security to the princes** who surrendered their sovereignty.
 
• The privy purses were paid as compensation for **merging their states** into the Indian Union after independence in 1947.
 
• In 1971, the privy purses were **abolished** by the then Prime Minister Indira Gandhi through a constitutional amendment, citing reasons of equality and the need to end privileges.
 
• The abolition of privy purses marked a significant step in **eliminating feudal privileges** and ensuring a more egalitarian society.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Integration of Princely States:**

 
 
• India had over **500 princely states** at the time of independence in 1947.
 
• Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel and V.P. Menon played a key role in integrating these states into the Indian Union.
 
• The princely rulers agreed to the merger in exchange for privileges, including privy purses.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Basis:**
 
 
• The privy purses were guaranteed under **Article 291 of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• They were later abolished through the **26th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1971**.
 
 
 
• **Reasons for Abolition:**
 
 
• The Indian government argued that privy purses were inconsistent with the **socialist and democratic ideals** of the Constitution.
 
• The move was seen as a step towards **ending hereditary privileges** and promoting equality.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Abolition:**
 
 
• The abolition of privy purses led to financial difficulties for some former rulers but was widely hailed as a progressive measure.
 
• It reinforced India's commitment to **egalitarianism and democratic values**.

questions.question: Which global observance did UNESCO mark on 24 January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**International Day of Education**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **International Day of Education** is observed globally on **24 January** every year.
 
• It was proclaimed by the **United Nations General Assembly** in December 2018 to emphasize the role of education in peace and development.
 
• UNESCO leads the global observance of this day, focusing on ensuring inclusive and equitable quality education for all as part of the **Sustainable Development Goal 4** (SDG 4).
 
• The theme for 2025 will highlight the importance of **transformative education** in addressing global challenges such as climate change, inequality, and poverty.
 
• The day serves as a call to action to prioritize education in policy-making and funding globally, aiming to build resilient and sustainable societies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Education as a Human Right:**

 
 
• The **Universal Declaration of Human Rights (1948)** recognizes education as a fundamental human right under Article 26.
 
• It emphasizes that primary education should be free and compulsory for all children.
 
 
 
• **Sustainable Development Goal 4:**
 
 
• SDG 4 aims to ensure inclusive and equitable quality education and promote lifelong learning opportunities for all by 2030.
 
• Key targets include universal primary and secondary education, vocational training, and eliminating gender disparities in access to education.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO’s Role:**
 
 
• UNESCO leads global efforts to advance education as a tool for peace, sustainable development, and social equity.
 
• It supports member states in implementing educational policies and frameworks aligned with global goals.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Global Education:**
 
 
• An estimated **244 million children and youth** were out of school globally as of 2023.
 
• Barriers include poverty, gender inequality, conflict, and lack of infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Transformative Education:**
 
 
• Transformative education focuses on empowering learners to become active participants in addressing global challenges.
 
• It integrates critical thinking, digital literacy, and environmental awareness into curricula.

questions.question: Most of the Thar desert lies within India, spanning the states of _________

options.text: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Uttar Pradesh
Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Madhya Pradesh
Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Himachal Pradesh

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is predominantly located in the northwestern region of India.
 
• It spans across the Indian states of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana, making it a significant geographical feature in these areas.
 
• The desert covers approximately 77,000 square miles (200,000 square kilometers), with Rajasthan accounting for the majority of its land area.
 
• It is characterized by arid conditions, sand dunes, sparse vegetation, and extreme temperatures, making it one of the most inhospitable regions in India.
 
• The Thar Desert also extends into Pakistan, but the majority of its area lies within Indian territory.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Climate of the Thar Desert:**

 
 
• The Thar Desert experiences an arid climate with very low rainfall, typically less than 200mm annually.
 
• Temperatures can soar above 50°C in the summer and drop below freezing in the winter.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Significance:**
 
 
• The desert hosts unique flora and fauna adapted to its harsh conditions, including desert foxes, camels, and khejri trees.
 
• The Desert National Park located in Rajasthan is a protected area that showcases the biodiversity of the region.
 
 
 
• **Human Settlement:**
 
 
• The Thar Desert is one of the world's most densely populated deserts, with villages scattered across its landscape.
 
• Traditional occupations in the region include camel breeding, agriculture (using irrigation), and handicrafts.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Features:**
 
 
• Sand dunes, salt pans, and rocky outcrops are prominent features of the Thar Desert's terrain.
 
• The Luni River is the only major river flowing through the desert region.

questions.question: Which canal project plays a major role in irrigation in the Thar Desert?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indira Gandhi Canal**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Indira Gandhi Canal** is one of the largest canal systems in India, and it plays a vital role in providing water for irrigation in the **Thar Desert** region.
 
• The canal originates at the **Harike Barrage**, located at the confluence of the Sutlej and Beas rivers in Punjab, and flows through Rajasthan.
 
• It was commissioned in **1984** and provides water to the arid regions of **western Rajasthan**, including Jodhpur, Bikaner, and surrounding areas.
 
• The canal irrigates around **19 lakh hectares** of land, transforming barren areas into fertile agricultural lands in the desert.
 
• The project has significantly contributed to the socio-economic development of the region, ensuring food security and better livelihoods for farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Thar Desert:**

 
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the **Great Indian Desert**, is the 17th largest desert in the world and covers approximately **200,000 square kilometers**.
 
• It spans the states of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana, with **Rajasthan** having the largest share.
 
• It is characterized by **extreme arid conditions**, high temperatures, and low rainfall (100-200 mm annually).
 
 
 
• **Harike Barrage:**
 
 
• The Harike Barrage is located in Punjab and serves as the source of the Indira Gandhi Canal.
 
• The barrage helps regulate the water flow from the **Sutlej and Beas rivers** into the canal system.
 
 
 
• **Water Management in Arid Regions:**
 
 
• The Indira Gandhi Canal project demonstrates how **large-scale irrigation systems** can combat desertification and promote agricultural activities in arid regions.
 
• It is an example of utilizing **inter-basin water transfer** to address water scarcity.
 
 
 
• **Economic Impact:**
 
 
• The Indira Gandhi Canal has boosted agriculture, created employment opportunities, and improved the quality of life for people in western Rajasthan.
 
• It has facilitated the cultivation of crops such as wheat, mustard, and cotton, which were previously impossible in the desert environment.

questions.question: What kind of architectural style is seen in the shikharas of the Jageshwar temple complexes in Uttarakhand, India?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Curvilinear shikharas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Jageshwar temple complexes in Uttarakhand are renowned for their **Nagara-style architecture**, which is characterized by curvilinear shikharas (spires).
 
• Curvilinear shikharas are distinctively tall and tapering structures that rise upwards in a convex curve and are a hallmark of North Indian temple architecture.
 
• Jageshwar temples primarily date back to the 7th to 12th centuries CE, showcasing intricate stone carvings and traditional designs.
 
• The shikharas of these temples often have an amalaka (circular disc-like structure) at the top, symbolizing divine energy and protection.
 
• The temple complex consists of over 100 small and large shrines dedicated to Lord Shiva, reflecting the religious significance of the region.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nagara Style Architecture:**

 
 
• This style is predominant in northern India and is characterized by curvilinear shikharas and multiple smaller towers surrounding the main temple.
 
• Unlike Dravidian architecture, Nagara temples do not have elaborate gateways (gopurams) and often feature intricate carvings on stone.
 
 
 
• **Amalaka:**
 
 
• The amalaka is a distinctive circular stone disc found atop the shikhara, symbolizing purity and spiritual protection.
 
• It is often surmounted by a kalasha (pot-like structure), adding to the aesthetic and symbolic significance of the temple.
 
 
 
• **Jageshwar Temple Complex:**
 
 
• Located in the Almora district of Uttarakhand, this complex is considered one of the oldest centers of Shaivism in India.
 
• The temples are surrounded by dense deodar forests, contributing to their serene and spiritual ambiance.
 
 
 
• **Historical Importance:**
 
 
• The Jageshwar temples are believed to have been built during the Katyuri and Chand dynasties, showcasing the evolution of temple architecture.
 
• The complex has inscriptions and sculptures that provide insights into religious practices and artistic styles of ancient India.

questions.question: _____ recorded the highest population density in 2011, as per the 2011 Census of India.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**North East Delhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As per the **2011 Census of India**, North East Delhi recorded the **highest population density** in the country.
 
• North East Delhi had a population density of **37,346 persons per square kilometer**, making it the most densely populated district in India.
 
• Population density is calculated as the number of persons per square kilometer of land area.
 
• North East Delhi is part of the National Capital Territory (NCT) of Delhi, which is itself one of the most urbanized and densely populated regions in India.
 
• The high population density in this region is attributed to urbanization, migration, and the concentration of residential settlements in limited geographic space.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Population Density:**

 
 
• Population density is a key demographic indicator that reflects the number of people living in a unit area of land.

• **2011 Census of India:**

• The Mahalwari system was introduced in 1833 by the British East India Company during the administration of **Lord William Bentinck**.
 
• Under this system, the **village headman (or Pradhan)** was made responsible for collecting land revenue from the farmers on behalf of the British government.
 
• The revenue settlement was made collectively for the village or estate, which was referred to as the "Mahal."
 
• This system was primarily implemented in parts of **North-Western Provinces, Central Provinces, Punjab, and Uttar Pradesh**.

• The system combined elements of both the Zamindari and Ryotwari systems.
 
• Revenue rates were periodically revised, and the village collectively bore the responsibility of payment.
 
 
 
• **Zamindari System:**
 
 
• In this system, land revenue was collected by landlords (Zamindars) from the peasants and paid to the British government.
 
• It was introduced in Bengal, Bihar, and Odisha under the Permanent Settlement Act of 1793.
 
 
 
• **Ryotwari System:**
 
 
• Here, the settlement was directly made with the cultivators (Ryots), who were recognized as the owners of the land.
 
• It was primarily implemented in Madras, Bombay, and parts of Assam.
 
 
 
• **Purpose of Revenue Systems:**
 
 
• The primary objective of these systems was to extract maximum revenue for the British administration.
 
• However, these policies often led to exploitation and economic distress among Indian farmers.

• **Hydrocarbons:** Organic compounds consisting of hydrogen and carbon atoms. Common fuels like natural gas and propane are hydrocarbons.

• **Economic Causes:** Exploitative land revenue systems and destruction of traditional industries hurt Indian peasants and artisans.
 
• **Social and Religious Causes:** Reforms like the abolition of Sati and the introduction of the Widow Remarriage Act created distrust among conservative Indians.
 
 
 
• **Key Leaders of the Revolt:**
 
 
• Rani Lakshmibai in Jhansi, Tantia Tope in Kanpur, and Begum Hazrat Mahal in Lucknow played significant roles in leading the rebellion.
 
 
 
• **Outcome of the Revolt:**
 
 
• The revolt was eventually suppressed by the British, and the East India Company was abolished in 1858.
 
• India came under the direct control of the British Crown, marking the beginning of the British Raj.
 
 
 
• **Historical Significance:**
 
 
• The Revolt of 1857 is often regarded as India's First War of Independence, despite its failure.
 
• It sowed the seeds for future resistance movements against British colonial rule.

questions.question: Which of these agricultural regions is best known for rice-wheat cropping system?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indo-Gangetic Plains**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indo-Gangetic Plains are one of the most fertile agricultural regions in India, supporting the rice-wheat cropping system.
 
• This cropping system is practiced in states like Punjab, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, and Bihar due to favorable climate and soil conditions.
 
• Rice is grown during the Kharif season (monsoon) as it requires a significant amount of water, while wheat is cultivated in the Rabi season (winter).
 
• The alluvial soil of the Indo-Gangetic Plains, coupled with abundant water resources from rivers like the Ganga and its tributaries, makes the region ideal for this cropping system.
 
• This system contributes significantly to India's food security, with the region being called the "Granary of India."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharif Crops:**

 
 
• These are crops grown during the monsoon season (June to October) and include rice, maize, and millets.
 
• Rice is the most prominent Kharif crop in the Indo-Gangetic Plains due to the high water availability during this period.
 
 
 
• **Rabi Crops:**
 
 
• These are crops grown in the winter season (November to April), such as wheat, barley, and mustard.
 
• Wheat cultivation in the Rabi season complements rice, forming the rice-wheat cropping pattern in the Indo-Gangetic Plains.
 
 
 
• **Alluvial Soil:**
 
 
• The Indo-Gangetic Plains are rich in alluvial soil, brought by rivers like the Ganga, Yamuna, and their tributaries.
 
• This soil is highly fertile and suitable for growing a wide variety of crops, including rice and wheat.
 
 
 
• **Food Security in India:**
 
 
• The rice-wheat cropping system in the Indo-Gangetic Plains contributes significantly to India's food grain production.
 
• This region plays a critical role in ensuring food security for the country, feeding millions of people.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution:**
 
 
• The Indo-Gangetic Plains were a major beneficiary of the Green Revolution in the 1960s-70s, which introduced high-yield variety seeds and improved irrigation methods.
 
• This led to a significant increase in the productivity of rice and wheat in the region.

questions.question: According to the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992, which body functions as the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system, ensuring broad-based community participation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gram Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Gram Sabha is the cornerstone of the Panchayati Raj system as established by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992.
 
• It consists of all the registered voters of a village or a group of villages within the jurisdiction of a Panchayat.
 
• Gram Sabha ensures direct participation of the community in decision-making, empowering local governance.
 
• Key functions of the Gram Sabha include approving village development plans, monitoring the implementation of projects, and ensuring transparency in Panchayat operations.
 
• It serves as the ultimate authority in the Panchayati Raj system, promoting democratic decentralization at the grassroots level.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992:**

 
 
• This Act provided constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions, ensuring decentralized governance.
 
• It mandates the establishment of Gram Sabha in each village or group of villages.
 
• Three-tier structure of Panchayati Raj: Gram Panchayat (village level), Panchayat Samiti (block level), and Zila Parishad (district level).
 
 
 
• **Nyaya Panchayat:**
 
 
• Nyaya Panchayats are judicial bodies functioning to resolve minor disputes at the village level.
 
• They are distinct from Gram Panchayats and focus solely on justice delivery.
 
 
 
• **Zila Parishad:**
 
 
• Zila Parishad operates at the district level, coordinating activities between block-level Panchayats.
 
• It formulates development plans and oversees their implementation across the district.
 
 
 
• **Gram Panchayat:**
 
 
• Gram Panchayats are executive bodies at the village level responsible for implementing developmental schemes.
 
• They work under the supervision of the Gram Sabha.

questions.question: How many religious communities are covered under the 2019 Citizenship Amendment Act?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) 2019 covers **6 religious communities:** Hindus, Sikhs, Buddhists, Jains, Parsis, and Christians.
 
• The act aims to provide Indian citizenship to persecuted religious minorities from **Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Afghanistan** who entered India on or before **31 December 2014**.
 
• It applies to individuals who faced religious persecution in these countries and were forced to migrate to India.
 
• The CAA **excludes Muslims** from its purview, as it focuses on non-Muslim minorities.
 
• The law does not alter the existing process of acquiring citizenship for others but facilitates faster citizenship for persecuted minorities.

• **Definition of Citizenship:** Citizenship refers to the legal status granted to an individual by a country, entitling them to certain rights and responsibilities.
 
• **Religious Persecution:** It refers to systematic mistreatment or oppression based on religious beliefs, often forcing affected individuals to flee their country.
 
• **Countries Covered:** The CAA specifically applies to refugees from **Pakistan, Bangladesh, and Afghanistan**, which are predominantly Muslim-majority nations.
 
• **Criticism of CAA:** Critics argue that the act violates the secular fabric of the Indian Constitution by excluding Muslims and raises concerns about discrimination.
 
• **NRC Connection:** The CAA has been linked to the proposed National Register of Citizens (NRC), which aims to identify illegal immigrants. However, the relationship between the two remains a contentious issue.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences passed by a Sessions Judge requires mandatory confirmation by the High Court?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Capital punishment**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Capital punishment, also known as the death sentence, when passed by a Sessions Judge, requires **mandatory confirmation by the High Court** as per Section 366(1) of the Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC).
 
• The Sessions Judge cannot execute the death sentence unless it is confirmed by the High Court, ensuring a higher level of judicial scrutiny.
 
• This procedural safeguard is implemented to ensure that the decision to impose capital punishment undergoes rigorous evaluation to prevent miscarriage of justice.
 
• Capital punishment is considered the most severe form of punishment and is reserved for rarest of rare cases such as heinous crimes.
 
• The High Court reviews the legality, validity, and appropriateness of the death sentence passed by the Sessions Court before issuing confirmation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC):**

 
 
• The CrPC is the main legislation governing criminal procedures in India.
 
• Under Section 366(1), it mandates High Court confirmation for death sentences imposed by Sessions Judges.
 
 
 
• **Rare Cases Doctrine:**
 
 
• Capital punishment in India is awarded only in the "rarest of rare cases" as established by the Supreme Court in the landmark case of *Bachan Singh v. State of Punjab* (1980).
 
• This doctrine ensures that death sentences are given only for exceptionally heinous crimes with sufficient justification.
 
 
 
• **Judicial Safeguards:**
 
 
• Mandatory High Court confirmation acts as a safeguard against errors or biases in lower court decisions.
 
• It ensures that the decision undergoes detailed scrutiny by experienced judges.
 
 
 
• **Execution Process:**
 
 
• Once the High Court confirms the death sentence, the convict has the right to appeal to the Supreme Court.
 
• Additionally, the convict can file a mercy petition to the President of India under Article 72 of the Constitution or to the Governor under Article 161.

• Pushyamitra Shunga ruled mainly in the central Indian region and is known for his patronage of Brahmanical traditions, contrasting with the largely Buddhist Mauryan rulers.

• **Mauryan Empire:**

 
 
• Founded by Chandragupta Maurya in 321 BCE, it was one of the largest empires in ancient India.
 
• It reached its zenith under Ashoka, who embraced Buddhism and spread it across Asia.
 
• The Mauryan administration was highly centralized, with a well-organized bureaucracy.
 
 
 
• **Decline of the Mauryan Empire:**
 
 
• After Ashoka's death, the empire weakened due to succession issues and administrative inefficiencies.
 
• The later Mauryan rulers like Brihadratha were unable to maintain the empire's stability.
 
 
 
• **Shunga Dynasty:**
 
 
• Founded by Pushyamitra Shunga in 185 BCE after the assassination of Brihadratha.
 
• The Shunga dynasty is known for reviving Brahmanical traditions and opposing the spread of Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The transition from the Mauryan to the Shunga dynasty marks a significant shift in Indian history, especially in religious and administrative practices.

questions.question: Which among the following contains a collection of eight poetic anthologies from ancient Tamil literature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Ettuttokai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ettuttokai** (The Eight Anthologies) is a significant part of **Sangam literature**, representing ancient Tamil poetry.
 
• It contains eight collections of Tamil poems, showcasing the life, culture, and traditions of the Sangam period (circa 300 BCE to 300 CE).
 
• The eight anthologies include works such as **Ainkurunuru**, **Kurunthogai**, **Narrinai**, and **Paripadal**, among others.
 
• These poems predominantly focus on two themes—**akam** (love and relationships) and **puram** (war, valor, and ethics).
 
• The Ettuttokai, along with the **Pattuppattu** (The Ten Idylls), forms the core of Tamil Sangam literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sangam Literature:**

 
 
• Sangam literature refers to the body of Tamil literature created during the Sangam age (circa 300 BCE to 300 CE).
 
• It is named after the Tamil Sangams (assemblies of poets and scholars) that were believed to have existed in ancient Tamilakam.
 
• These works are considered the earliest examples of Tamil literature and provide valuable insights into the political, social, and cultural life of that period.
 
 
 
• **Akam and Puram:**
 
 
• **Akam** refers to the inner world of emotions, focusing on love, relationships, and personal experiences.
 
• **Puram** deals with the external world, including themes such as war, heroism, and societal duties.
 
 
 
• **Pattuppattu (The Ten Idylls):**
 
 
• It is another major collection of Sangam poetry, consisting of ten long poems.
 
• These poems complement the Ettuttokai in representing the literary richness of ancient Tamil culture.
 
 
 
• **Historical Importance:**
 
 
• The Sangam texts provide detailed accounts of the political, economic, and social structures of ancient Tamilakam.
 
• They are regarded as an invaluable source for understanding the history and evolution of South Indian civilization.

questions.question: What is the main advantage of saving an MS PowerPoint presentation as a .pdf file?

options.text: It allows all MS PowerPoint animations to run.
It reduces file size and prevents unwanted editing.
It enables users to modify slides in any PDF viewer.
It automatically translates text into different languages.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**It reduces file size and prevents unwanted editing.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Saving an MS PowerPoint presentation as a **.pdf file** ensures that the content becomes non-editable, thereby **preventing unauthorized modifications**.
 
• PDF files are generally more compact than PowerPoint files, which helps in **reducing file size** and making them easier to share.
 
• PDF format ensures **consistent display of content**, maintaining the original layout, fonts, and graphics regardless of the device or software used to view it.
 
• The PDF format is widely supported across various platforms and operating systems, providing **universal compatibility**.
 
• Saving as PDF removes PowerPoint-specific features such as animations and transitions, focusing solely on the core content for easy readability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **PDF (Portable Document Format):**

 
 
• Developed by Adobe, PDFs are designed to present documents in a manner independent of application software, hardware, or operating systems.
 
• PDFs support text, images, hyperlinks, and even forms, making them versatile for a variety of uses.
 
 
 
• **File Compression in PDFs:**
 
 
• PDF software often includes algorithms to compress images and remove redundant data, helping reduce overall file size.
 
 
 
• **Security Features of PDFs:**
 
 
• PDFs can be encrypted and password-protected to prevent unauthorized access.
 
• They also support permissions, allowing authors to restrict actions like printing or copying content.
 
 
 
• **Difference Between PPT and PDF:**
 
 
• PPT files are editable and support animations, transitions, and interactive elements, while PDFs are static and primarily focused on readability and sharing.
 
 
 
• **Universal Compatibility:**
 
 
• PDF viewers are available across all major operating systems, including Windows, macOS, Linux, and mobile platforms.

questions.question: With reference to the 40th Amendment Act, 1976, which category of maritime zones came under the legislative jurisdiction of the Parliament?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Territorial waters and EEZ**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The 40th Amendment Act, 1976, brought **Territorial waters, Continental Shelf, Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), and other maritime zones** under the legislative jurisdiction of the Parliament.
 
• This amendment added **Entry 25 to the Union List** in the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution of India, empowering Parliament to legislate on these areas.
 
• The aim was to align India's constitutional framework with **international maritime laws**, specifically the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS).
 
• The amendment reinforced India's **sovereign rights** over resources in these maritime zones, including fisheries, oil, and natural gas exploration.
 
• This was a crucial step in establishing a clear legal framework for India's maritime boundaries and jurisdiction over its waters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Territorial Waters:**

 
 
• Territorial waters extend up to **12 nautical miles** from the baseline of a coastal state.
 
• The state has **sovereignty** over these waters, including the airspace above and the seabed below.
 
 
 
• **Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ):**
 
 
• The EEZ extends up to **200 nautical miles** from the baseline.
 
• In this zone, the coastal state has **special rights** regarding the exploration and use of marine resources, including energy production from water and wind.
 
 
 
• **Continental Shelf:**
 
 
• The continental shelf is the seabed and subsoil that extends beyond the territorial waters, up to **200 nautical miles** or more, depending on geological criteria.
 
• The coastal state has sovereign rights for exploring and exploiting natural resources in this area.
 
 
 
• **United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea (UNCLOS):**
 
 
• UNCLOS, also known as the **Law of the Sea Treaty**, was adopted in **1982**.
 
• It defines maritime zones such as territorial waters, EEZ, and continental shelf and establishes the rights and responsibilities of nations regarding the use of oceans.
 
 
 
• **India's Maritime Claims:**
 
 
• India has a coastline of approximately **11,084** **km** and an EEZ of **2.37 million square kilometers**.
 
• The legislative jurisdiction over maritime zones enables India to safeguard its strategic, economic, and environmental interests.
